clue.text: A CD character I detect

explanation.surface: A character from a Conan Doyle story introduces himself by his trade.
explanation.walkthrough: CD stands for Conan Doyle, the author; the second definition is the character's own boast, 'I detect', since he is the great fictional detective.
explanation.definitionFit: Conan Doyle created the famous Baker Street sleuth, whose whole job is detection, so both halves point to the same consulting detective.

clue.text: Trouble in new refits

indicators.note: new suggests the letters of refits are made into something fresh, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Something goes wrong with newly refitted equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: Strife is conflict or discord, a kind of trouble between people.

clue.text: Book departure

definitions.meaning: the second book of the Old Testament
a mass going-out, as of the Israelites from Egypt

explanation.definitionFit: The Bible book is named for the Israelites' going out of Egypt, and the word also means any mass leaving.

clue.text: What tenant pays arises with sixth off in the future

indicators.note: sixth is an ordinal, an 'nth', so the letter N is taken off
in a down clue arising means the word climbs, so it is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a tenant pays rental to the landlord

explanation.surface: A tenant's payment goes up, with a sixth knocked off, at some future date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arises' turns RENTAL into LATNER; 'with sixth off' removes N, reading 'sixth' as an example of an nth, leaving the answer. The device is loose: no letter here is literally sixth.
explanation.definitionFit: Later means at a subsequent time, that is, at some point to come.

clue.text: Not applicable in group of players with a game

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the word for the players

parts.note: a cast is the company of actors in a play
NA is the standard abbreviation for not applicable on forms

explanation.surface: A form entry marked not applicable among a troupe of actors who play a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Players' suggests a card game's participants, but here they are actors: a CAST.
explanation.definitionFit: Canasta is a rummy-type card game played with two packs.

clue.text: See 1
Revolting attack

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an adjective for something disgusting and a noun for a military push forward.

clue.text: One can remember using it

parts.note: describes a device such as a rhyme or acronym that aids the memory

explanation.definitionFit: A mnemonic is a memory aid, such as a rhyme for the planets' order.

clue.text: Thinks false as those considered by 1,5?

definitions.meaning: the people a detective has under suspicion in a case

explanation.surface: A character's doubt about the people the famous detective is investigating.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means doubts someone's honesty; as a noun it names the possible culprits a detective weighs up.

clue.text: Ros got in muddle settling down

indicators.note: in muddle says the letters of the three words before are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A woman named Ros got into a mess while trying to settle down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is part of the anagram fodder as well as sitting before 'muddle': the eight letters of ROS GOT IN are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds roosting are perching to rest for the night, settling down to sleep.

clue.text: English river in fast flowing course

indicators.note: in places the two abbreviations inside the rearranged word
flowing suggests the letters of fast move about freely, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: An English river runs along a swift watercourse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flowing' turns FAST into AFTS, and 'in' puts ER inside it. 'Course' looks like a river's path but is a course of a meal; AFTERS is British slang for dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: Afters is British informal for pudding, the sweet course that follows the main dish.

clue.text: Not so much of what's read at service? Not on

indicators.note: Not here tells you to leave out the following word from the passage just named

parts.note: a lesson is a Bible passage read aloud at church
taken as written

explanation.surface: A churchgoer hopes for a shorter reading at the service, or none at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Less means a smaller amount, a lower quantity than before.

clue.text: Infection round residence the church's to bring to light

parts.note: flu is influenza, a viral infection
O is round in shape
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: An illness around the vicarage is something the church wants to expose.
explanation.walkthrough: CE, Church of England, is the established church in England.
explanation.definitionFit: To fluoresce is to give off visible light under radiation, glowing as if lit up.

clue.text: Bond returns in the sooner the better

indicators.note: returns says the hidden run is read backwards
in tells you the letters lie within the words that follow

explanation.surface: James Bond comes back as soon as possible, ideally.
explanation.walkthrough: Bond looks like 007, but it is a tie: a loop of rope.
explanation.definitionFit: A noose is a loop of rope that ties, a kind of bond or snare.

clue.text: Bones discovered in the Trossachs

indicators.note: discovered in says the letters are found inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Ancient bones were unearthed in a Scottish beauty spot.
explanation.walkthrough: The Trossachs is a wooded glen area in central Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Ossa is the Latin plural of os, the anatomical word for bone.

clue.text: Psychiatrist era in contraction?

parts.note: shrink is slang for a psychiatrist, from headshrinker
an age is an era, a period of history

explanation.surface: A psychiatrist working in a particular period of history.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrinkage is the amount by which something reduces in size, a contraction.

clue.text: I bring certain sportsmen to the top

definitions.text: I bring certain sportsmen to the top

parts.words: I bring certain sportsmen to the top
parts.note: read not as a coach promoting athletes but as a machine carrying skiers up a slope

explanation.surface: A coach boasts of taking athletes to the summit of their sport.
explanation.definitionFit: A ski lift is a cable-hauled chair or tow that carries skiers up the mountain.

clue.text: The player in it should have it!

definitions.text: The player in it should have it!

parts.words: The player in it should have it!
parts.note: the same two words name both the society a golfer joins and the stick a golfer swings

explanation.definitionFit: A golfer belongs to an association of players and also carries the iron or wood used to hit the ball.

clue.text: Period of decay following success at the end of the day

definitions.meaning: the declining years after a career's peak

definitions.text: at the end of the day
definitions.meaning: the dim light just after sunset

explanation.surface: A fading career after its triumphs, ending as night falls.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means the dusk after sunset and, figuratively, a time of decline after a heyday.

clue.text: Where nurses are ahead

definitions.meaning: nurses work out on the hospital's patient rooms, split as two words

explanation.surface: Nurses press forward on the wards.
explanation.definitionFit: Split in two, the letters say nurses are in hospital rooms; as one word they mean forward, ahead.

clue.text: Quantity of money laid on ring for wrestling

indicators.note: laid on in a down clue puts the first piece on top of the second

parts.note: a sum is an amount of money
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A sum of money is staked on a ring for a wrestling bout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring' looks like the wrestling arena, but it gives the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Sumo is the Japanese style of heavyweight wrestling.

clue.text: Bearing people around island

indicators.note: around tells you the word for people encloses the abbreviation

parts.note: men are people

explanation.surface: People carrying something round an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Mien is a person's look or manner, their bearing or demeanour.

clue.text: Transport round northern island for one with responsibility

indicators.note: round says the word for transport goes around the two abbreviations

parts.note: a motor is a car, a means of transport

explanation.surface: A vehicle tours a northern island, driven by someone in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: A school monitor is a pupil given duties, someone entrusted with a responsibility.

clue.text: Robin flying over heart of wood. Bad luck?

indicators.note: flying over in a down clue sets the first piece above the next

parts.note: Robin Hood, the outlaw of Sherwood Forest

indicators.note: heart of picks the middle letters of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A robin flies above the middle of a forest, an omen of misfortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Robin' looks like the bird but is Robin Hood, giving HOOD.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoodoo is a jinx, something bringing misfortune.

clue.text: The remains of a brief agenda

indicators.note: of says the answer is made from part of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Only the leftover items of a short meeting agenda remain.
explanation.definitionFit: A fag end is British slang for a cigarette stub, and by extension the leftover last part of anything.

clue.text: Half the city in pursuit of fellow English criminal

indicators.note: in pursuit of means the city half follows behind the abbreviations
Half tells you to keep only one of the two halves of the word for the city

parts.note: London is the city in British puzzles

explanation.surface: In the city, half the force chases an English villain.
explanation.definitionFit: A felon is a person convicted of a serious crime.

clue.text: The state of Maine's not in contention

indicators.note: in contention suggests the letters are in conflict and scrambled

explanation.surface: Maine claims it is not in the running in some contest.
explanation.walkthrough: Maine is a red herring: the answer is a different US state, made from the letters of MAINE'S NOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Minnesota is a US state in the upper Midwest.

clue.text: Precise but unsatisfactory EC tax

indicators.note: unsatisfactory suggests the letters are in a poor order needing rearrangement

explanation.surface: A European Community tax is precise but flawed.
explanation.definitionFit: Exact means accurate in every detail, precise.

clue.text: Hold-up with wood stick

parts.note: a log is a piece of wood
to jam is to stick fast

explanation.surface: A holdup caused by wood that is stuck.
explanation.definitionFit: A logjam is a blockage, literally of floating timber and so any standstill.

clue.text: Jockey will appear to take both sides

definitions.text: Jockey will appear to take both sides

parts.words: Jockey will appear to take both sides
parts.note: a rider sits with one leg on each side of the horse, which also means not committing to either side of an argument

explanation.definitionFit: To straddle is to sit astride with a leg either side, or to favour both sides of an issue.

clue.text: A CD character (in DC!)

parts.note: CD is Charles Dickens and DC is his novel David Copperfield, in which this aunt appears

explanation.definitionFit: Dickens created the formidable great-aunt who takes in the young hero of David Copperfield.
